page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core allocation managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ams_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test places the server in the top 10% of benchmarked instances with a score of 147,761.02, while the single-core performance scores 3,080.17. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 226.16 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 144.16 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 and software compilation with clang both rank in the top 10%, scoring 626.48 GB/sec and 65,929.0 respectively. For database workloads, the server processes 112.7 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 29,698.89 on PassMark database operations.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between compute-intensive tasks and large-scale model execution. While small to medium language model inference performs well, achieving 42.31 tokens/sec for text generation on a 7B model, performance drops to average levels for large 70B models, yielding 4.83 tokens/sec. The lack of local storage requires external premium storage attachment, which influences overall architectural cost efficiency. Given its high memory-to-core ratio and strong multi-threaded processing, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale language model inference.
